note: Curly apostrophe (U+2019) and en dash (U+2013) as they appear in committed locators; both are tokenizer separators, and neither reaches the corpus text itself (FR-2: normalization applies only to router documents and queries).
The same curly apostrophe inside running prose; 'the'/'on' are stopwords and 'lying' stems to 'ly'.
U+FB01/U+FB02 ligatures from older public-domain transcriptions decompose under NFKC before stemming.
Fullwidth Latin folds to ASCII under NFKC, then casefolds.

NFKC does not strip combining accents, so accented letters split the token at the tokenizer; recorded as the committed behaviour rather than silently 'fixed', because changing it would change every routing score.
En-dashed folio range of a reference_only locator.
The tokenizer splits contractions; 'don' and 't' are stopwords, so only the content word survives.
Vocabulary the taxonomy has never seen, normalized identically to everything else — this is what the FR-4 coverage signal measures.
